subject: Landing zone actions & rotation plan for QBR readiness
content:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Park <andrew@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Landing zone actions & rotation plan for QBR readiness

Team —

Quick sync notes and asks after this morning’s xfn call with Acme. Goal: make the QBR packet and the demo runway predictable and remove the three open exec blockers by the end of next week. I’ve attached an updated checklist and the mutual action plan we walked through.

Topline asks (owners + deadlines):
- Action A: Finalize the trimmed demo prompt set and golden example outputs — Owner: Marissa — Tue 09/28 EOD
- Action B: Confirm production routing policy for Acme traffic (dedicated vs hosted fallback) — Owner: Karthik — Wed 09/29 11:59 PDT
- Action C: Provide SOC2 evidence snapshot and data retention summary for procurement — Owner: Kimberly — Fri 10/01 5pm PDT
- Action D: Validate QBR slide deck numbers (latency / cost / error rates) with telemetry team — Owner: Jonas (+ telemetry) — Thu 09/30 noon PDT

Please update the checklist (QBR_landing_zone_checklist_v3.xlsx) with any sub-tasks and mark items you need help with. I’m looping Andrew on timing items so Acme can surface any procurement constraints early.

Two additional notes:
- If we can’t meet the routing policy decision by Wed, we will default to a staged roll that pins Acme to Dedicated with a 72-hr warmup and automated fallback to the latest hosted variant. That should be our contingency; Karthik please confirm whether that is operationally feasible.
- Marissa — the demo prompt set should include at least two edge-case prompts where caching/quantization changes impact quality; mark those as holdouts.

Thanks — small, focused wins here will reduce exec-level risk. I’ll collate status tomorrow morning before the 10am leadership readout.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Park <andrew@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 11:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing zone actions & rotation plan for QBR readiness

Thanks Vivek — taking Action A. Quick status:
- I trimmed the prompt corpus down to 18 core prompts and flagged 4 holdouts (edge-case quant/kv-cache behaviors). Will attach the final list to the checklist by EOD Monday.
- Need a short test harness from infra to run the edge-case prompts under the same quantization profile we plan to ship; Karthik, can infra stand up a short-run by Tues morning?

Small ask: can we prioritize the demo for the leadership readout to show both a high-throughput and a low-latency path? That helps the execs see the cost/latency tradeoff live.

MARISSA COLE
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Andrew Park <andrew@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 13:40:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing zone actions & rotation plan for QBR readiness

Can confirm on routing fallback plan — operationally we can do the staged pin to Dedicated with fallback to hosted, but two constraints:
1) Warmup: 48–72 hours for cache warming to get predictable latency on the Dedicated pool. If Acme requires immediate low latency day-one, we need to commit burst capacity for the first 72 hours.
2) SLA adjustment: we’ll need a temporary exception in the routing policy to allow cross-region fallback for redundancy; I’ll file the request with infra and procurement today.

Infra can spin up a small harness for Marissa — I’ll assign a runner and post the test job link to the Drive folder by Monday morning.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime

---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Park <andrew@acme-analytics.com>, marketplace-team@cloudpartner.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Landing zone actions & rotation plan for QBR readiness

Closing loop on Action D — I pulled the last 30 days of telemetry for the Acme account and aligned the summary numbers with finance. Two immediate items:
- We saw a 12% median latency delta for long-context flows when we tested the quantized variant; I’ll put the detailed chart in the Drive link and flag the top 3 queries that drive the delta.
- Cost math for the staged Dedicated roll (with burst) is in the HubSpot deal notes — I’ll add a short one-pager to the checklist.

Kimberly — any update on SOC2 evidence items? If procurement needs a signed attestation, we should schedule a 30-min call with Acme legal next week.

I’ll update the checklist now and mark my subtasks. If anyone needs me to push numbers into the QBR slide draft I can do that tonight.

Jonas Weber
Principal Growth Analyst, Redwood Inference
